wide.headline: In 1,000 profit-blind wallets, past winners do not stay ahead, but past losers keep losing.

rows.bets: Top earners on the profit leaderboard

readout: Track records do persist across 1,000 wallets, but almost entirely on the losing side: the worst third by older edge keeps losing about 2 points per bet.
The best third by older edge roughly breaks even afterwards. No group showed a reliably positive future edge.
The profit leaderboard carries no persistent signal.

title: On Polymarket sports, apparent trader skill does not persist once already-decided bets are removed
question: Does a wallet's edge against the price it paid in its older bets predict its edge in its newer bets?

rows.note: Wallets repeatedly buying outcomes already decided, such as at 98 cents

rows.sample: Top earners on the profit leaderboard

readout: The first run's persistence came from wallets that repeatedly buy outcomes that are already decided. That earns a small steady edge, but it is not forecasting.
Once those bets are removed, no group of wallets shows edge that carries over from older to newer bets, pre-game or in-play.
The profit leaderboard is no better: the past edge of top earners does not predict their future edge.
caveats: 65 wallets, one split per wallet; wallets trade the same events, so they are not independent.
Real skill smaller than about 3 points per bet cannot be detected per wallet at these sample sizes; cohort-level tests with many more wallets could detect it.
